artifact_revision: agentmux ab5e1245 + session-13 working tree: Agent Mux.app Debug build of it (run as a copy with bundle identifier io.github.sglavoie.agentmux.acceptance13) and amx 0.8.0 built from it into an isolated bin; embedded Ghostty 1.3.1 (GhosttyKit pinned in macos/GHOSTTY_VERSION); Kitty 0.49.1; tmux 3.7c on AgentMux's private server; installed asl; macOS 27.0.1
method: Two layers. (1) The hosted XCTest suite (`just mac-test`, 311 tests, 0 failures; 22 new in WorkspaceSidebarTests, WorkspaceWindowTests, WorkspaceStreamTests) and four Go tests for the daemon change this session needed. (2) A live run of the real app on this machine in an isolated world under /tmp/amxs13 (own HOME, TMPDIR, config, daemon, runtime-session registry, private tmux server, ASL state, and a separate Kitty instance with its own socket), so the operator's daemon, tmux, Kitty, config, and installed Agent Mux.app were never used. The app under test is this working tree's Debug build copied under another bundle identifier, which gives it its own preferences and lets it run beside the installed app. It was driven from outside: real left clicks (CGEvent) on sidebar rows, keys through System Events, the status-item menu, the Session menu, and the answer panel's Reply button through accessibility presses, and the app copy's own global shortcuts (⌃⌥⇧⌘N, ⌃⌥⇧⌘D) pressed as key events while another app was frontmost. It was observed from outside: the sidebar and panes read through accessibility, the app's unified log, the private tmux server's client list and pane contents, the runtime-session registry, `kitten @ ls` on the separate Kitty, the frontmost process, the daemon's v2 snapshot read by a second subscriber, and window screenshots. Every condition is a PASS/FAIL line in session-13/workspace-acceptance.log (117 PASS, 0 FAIL in the recorded pass). Stand-ins, stated plainly: the harness is a shell script named claude (no model, no network) that sends real hooks through `amx hook-indicator` on typed commands, echoes anything else typed, and, as an `asl run` worker, asks one real mailbox question and completes after the reply. Two world-only shims: Kitty and libghostty both start commands through login(1), which resets HOME, so the Kitty tabs get a private ZDOTDIR and the app copy runs amx through a three-line wrapper that puts the world's HOME back. Real: the app, its embedded Ghostty terminals running `amx attach`, Kitty, tmux, the daemon, the registry, and the installed asl with its hooks and bridge. Not exercised live: a real Claude/Codex/Copilot agent, physical keyboard and mouse, notification banners (the copy's notification backend was off to avoid a permission prompt; the banner-to-workspace path has a unit test only), the Preferences window, a Release build of the app, two Kitty instances at once, sleep/wake, and Reattach after another terminal takes a session (hosted tests only). Two earlier full passes were discarded: one stopped at the ASL step because the setup script had linked `asl` to itself, and one passed completely but an unrelated desktop alert covered its screenshots; the recorded pass repeats it from a rebuilt world with the window moved clear. Finding fixed in this session: the daemon's v2 snapshot listed tmux sessions with no project or profile, so the sidebar could not group them; the daemon now labels them (internal/daemon/runtime_labels.go). Finding left open: after an embedded view closes, tmux has no client but the registry still shows the attachment record until the next attach replaces it.

project-profile-sidebar.evidence: With two tmux sessions of project alpha (profiles work and personal) and one Kitty session of project beta, the real app's sidebar, read through accessibility, listed exactly five rows: the project line alpha, then 'alpha, personal' and 'alpha, work', then the project line beta, then 'beta, work … Kitty'. The daemon's v2 snapshot read by a second subscriber listed the same three sessions with project and profile, the tmux ones by runtime session and pane. After the stand-in in alpha/personal and the one in the Kitty tab each raised a permission prompt, the rows read 'alpha, personal, needs attention' and 'beta, work, needs attention', their cells showed 🔑 where alpha/work kept ⚡, each project line showed a waiting count of 1, and the status item's title read '⚡1 🔑2'; after both resumed no row needed attention. Artifacts: session-13/workspace-acceptance.log (S1, S2), session-13/sidebar-attention.png. Unit and hosted coverage: WorkspaceSidebarTests (grouping, ordering, labels, v2 decoding) and WorkspaceWindowTests.testSidebarListsProjectsThenTheirSessions in session-13/xcodebuild-test.log; the daemon labeling in session-13/go-test-labels.log.

mixed-backend-focus.evidence: A real click on alpha/work made the app attach a terminal (log: 'attached a terminal to rs-…', 'focus embedded rs-…'); the private tmux server then had one client on that pane with term xterm-ghostty, the registry recorded the attachment, the window title became 'alpha — work', and text typed with no further click appeared in that agent's pane ('echo[4]: typed-into-work'). A click on alpha/personal attached a second terminal (two Ghostty clients), typed text reached only that agent, and clicking back on alpha/work focused it with the same two clients and no new attachment. A click on the Kitty session beta/work logged 'focus Kitty window 2 externally'; `kitten @ ls` showed beta's window focused where tab 1 had been active, the separate Kitty process became the frontmost app, the tmux client list was unchanged (nothing embedded), and the workspace pane read 'beta runs in Kitty'. Artifacts: session-13/workspace-acceptance.log (F1–F3), session-13/focus-embedded.png, session-13/focus-kitty.png. Hosted coverage: WorkspaceWindowTests (one terminal per session, hidden not closed, arrow-key selection never raises Kitty, Show in Kitty) in session-13/xcodebuild-test.log.

next-attention.evidence: Three sessions were made to wait in a known order: alpha/personal (tmux), beta/work (Kitty), alpha/work (tmux). With the separate Kitty frontmost on another tab, the app copy's global shortcut was pressed. First press: log 'next attention: tmux %1 (key)', the workspace focused that session's embedded terminal, the app became frontmost, and the sidebar selection was alpha/personal with a Ghostty client on its pane. Second press: 'next attention: window 2 (key)', Kitty focused beta's window and became frontmost. Third press, over Kitty: 'next attention: tmux %0 (key)', the app frontmost on alpha/work, and typed text reached that agent. Fourth press wrapped to alpha/personal; the Session menu's Next Needing Attention then continued the same cycle to the Kitty window. After alpha/work resumed, presses alternated between the two remaining sessions and never chose it; with nothing waiting the log read 'next attention: nothing is waiting'. Artifacts: session-13/workspace-acceptance.log (A1–A6), session-13/next-attention.png. Unit coverage: WorkspaceSidebarTests.testNextAttentionCyclesAcrossBackendsOldestFirst (including two Kitty instances) in session-13/xcodebuild-test.log.

daemon-reconnect.evidence: With alpha/work selected and focused and alpha/personal attached behind it, the world's daemon was stopped. The app logged 'rows held from the last snapshot (3 session(s), selection rs-…)' and 'feed: notRunning'; the sidebar still listed the same five rows with the same selection, dimmed, with 'Daemon: not running' under them; the tmux client list was identical (same client pids); text typed then still reached alpha/work's agent, and alpha/personal could be selected and typed into from the held rows. After the daemon was started again the app logged 'feed: live' and 'rows current (3 session(s), selection rs-…)'; the sidebar read the same, grouped and labeled as before with the same selection, the notice was gone, the tmux clients and the agents' pids were unchanged, the log held no attach, detach, or 'no longer listed' line, and typed text still reached alpha/work. The new daemon's first v2 snapshot already carried project and profile for both tmux sessions, and a prompt raised afterwards marked the same row. Artifacts: session-13/workspace-acceptance.log (R1–R4), session-13/daemon-down.png, session-13/daemon-back.png. Hosted coverage: WorkspaceStreamTests.testSidebarAndTerminalsStayConsistentAcrossAReconnect (socket to sidebar with real Ghostty surfaces across a dropped stream) and WorkspaceWindowTests reconnect cases in session-13/xcodebuild-test.log.

retained-menu-shortcuts-asl.evidence: With the workspace open, the status item's menu (read through accessibility) still held the Needs attention and Working sections with the tmux and Kitty sessions, then Open Workspace, Open Dashboard, Launch Project, Recent, Notifications, Preferences…, and Quit Agent Mux; pressing the tmux session's menu row focused it in the workspace. The dashboard global shortcut logged 'dashboard opened (window N)' and brought the separate Kitty forward on a new dashboard tab. A real `asl run` started inside the tmux session alpha/work had its worker ask a mailbox question; after `asl outbox wait` surfaced it as that session, the daemon's snapshot listed the run waiting on that runtime session, the sidebar row read needs attention, and the status menu offered Answer… under the row. Pressing it logged 'answer panel: run …' and opened the Supervisor question panel over the workspace showing the plan name and 'Proceed with the fixture change?'; text typed into its editor enabled Reply, and Reply logged 'asl_action … accepted'. The worker's `asl ask` returned with exactly that reply text and exit 0, the daemon stopped listing the run as waiting, and the panel closed itself. Closing the workspace window then left no tmux client and the same live agent processes, and Open Workspace in the status menu brought it back on the remembered session. Artifacts: session-13/workspace-acceptance.log (M1–M3, C1–C2), session-13/asl-answer-panel.png, session-13/workspace-after-answer.png. Unchanged suites still passing in session-13/xcodebuild-test.log: MenuBuilderTests, ActionGateTests, HotKeyTests, ASLQuestionFlowTests, ASLResponseStateTests, NotificationPresenterTests; new: WorkspaceSidebarTests.testMenuListsTmuxSessionsWithTheirAnswerItems.
